title: Les familles de participes passés et leurs auxiliaires
summary: Report discoveries, journeys and encounters with connu, paru, couru, battu and apparu.
objectives: Build compound past forms across four irregular families.
Distinguish the usual auxiliaries of paraître, apparaître and naître.

sources.label: B1 public topic index (coverage reference only)

sections.title: A present auxiliary plus a family participle
paragraphs: The passé composé combines an auxiliary, a helping verb, with a past participle. With avoir, learn j'ai, tu as, il/elle/on a, nous avons, vous avez, ils/elles ont. The participle does not agree with the subject. Agreement with a preceding direct object is a separate rule; our examples keep direct objects after the verb.

Connaître gives connu; reconnaître gives reconnu and méconnaître gives méconnu (to misunderstand or fail to recognize). Paraître gives paru; disparaître gives disparu, reparaître gives reparu and comparaître gives comparu (to appear in court). These are not regular -u forms derived by mechanically cutting off -aître.

Courir gives couru; parcourir gives parcouru (to travel through or cover), accourir gives accouru (to rush over), recourir gives recouru (to resort to) and secourir gives secouru (to help or rescue). Accourir can also take être; the exercises specifying avoir train that accepted pattern. Battre gives battu; combattre gives combattu, débattre gives débattu and abattre gives abattu. Se battre is reflexive and therefore uses être: elle s'est battue.
points: The complete base paradigms below make each auxiliary and participle visible. The named derivatives use the same six avoir forms with their own listed participle.
Vocabulary: un parcours (masculine), a route; un témoin (masculine), a witness; une panne (feminine), a breakdown.

examples.french:
j'**ai connu**
tu **as connu**
il/elle/on **a connu**
nous **avons connu**
vous **avez connu**
ils/elles **ont connu**
examples.english:
I knew / have known
you knew / have known (singular)
he/she/one knew / has known
we knew / have known
you knew / have known (plural or polite)
they knew / have known
examples.note: Use for an experience or bounded period of knowing; ongoing past familiarity often takes connaissais.

examples.french:
j'**ai paru**
tu **as paru**
il/elle/on **a paru**
nous **avons paru**
vous **avez paru**
ils/elles **ont paru**
examples.english:
I seemed / have seemed
you seemed / have seemed (singular)
he/she/one seemed / has seemed
we seemed / have seemed
you seemed / have seemed (plural or polite)
they seemed / have seemed
examples.note: This is the avoir paradigm for paraître meaning seem. Publication can also use être, as explained below.

examples.french:
j'**ai couru**
tu **as couru**
il/elle/on **a couru**
nous **avons couru**
vous **avez couru**
ils/elles **ont couru**
examples.english:
I ran / have run
you ran / have run (singular)
he/she/one ran / has run
we ran / have run
you ran / have run (plural or polite)
they ran / have run
examples.note: Couru remains unchanged for these subjects with avoir.

examples.french:
j'**ai battu**
tu **as battu**
il/elle/on **a battu**
nous **avons battu**
vous **avez battu**
ils/elles **ont battu**
examples.english:
I beat / have beaten
you beat / have beaten (singular)
he/she/one beat / has beaten
we beat / have beaten
you beat / have beaten (plural or polite)
they beat / have beaten
examples.note: Use this pattern for beating a record or opponent; se battre is a different, reflexive construction.
Recognizing is a completed event here.

examples.french: La panne **a paru** moins grave après le contrôle.
examples.english: The breakdown seemed less serious after the inspection.

examples.note: No subject agreement on parcouru with avoir.

examples.french: Les élus **ont débattu** de la proposition.
examples.english: The elected representatives debated the proposal.
The volunteers helped a cyclist in distress.

mistakes.why: Avoir does not make the participle agree with the subject.
Battre has the irregular participle battu.

sections.title: Apparu and né: do not choose by spelling alone
paragraphs: Apparaître gives apparu and is normally used with être in contemporary French. Avoir is also attested, especially when emphasizing the event; it is not an impossible form. The exercises request être where a single auxiliary is expected. With être, the participle agrees with the subject: apparu, apparue, apparus, apparues.

Naître gives né and takes être: je suis né/née, tu es né/née, il/on est né, elle est née, nous sommes nés/nées, vous êtes né/née/nés/nées according to the people addressed, ils sont nés, elles sont nées. The participle rené of renaître is rare, literary or historical recognition material, not a recommended compound form for ordinary learner or TCF production; use an everyday paraphrase such as a repris vie, came back to life, where appropriate. Renaître is not a paraître-family verb. For publications, paraître can also take être to present the published state: le livre est paru. Do not turn the common avoir pattern into an absolute ban on être.
points: On uses est; agreement can reflect a known group when on means we.
With polite vous addressing one person, agreement remains singular.

examples.french:
je **suis apparu/apparue**
tu **es apparu/apparue**
il **est apparu** / elle **est apparue** / on **est apparu**
nous **sommes apparus/apparues**
vous **êtes apparu/apparue/apparus/apparues**
ils **sont apparus** / elles **sont apparues**
examples.english:
I appeared
you appeared (singular)
he appeared / she appeared / one appeared
we appeared
you appeared (polite singular or plural)
they appeared (masculine or mixed) / they appeared (feminine)
examples.note: Choose one agreement form to match the actual subject; slashes show alternatives, not a sentence to say aloud.

examples.french: Deux nouvelles options **sont apparues** à l'écran.
examples.english: Two new options appeared on the screen.
My sister was born in Rennes.
examples.note: Naître has its own participle and takes être.

examples.french: Le deuxième volume **est paru** en juin.
examples.english: The second volume came out in June.
examples.note: Être is accepted for publication; a paru is also possible.

mistakes.why: With être, agree apparues with the feminine plural subject.

practice.prompt: Supply the past participle of connaître: J'ai ___ cette période difficile.
practice.explanation: Connaître gives connu.

practice.prompt: Supply courir in the passé composé: Nous ___ jusqu'à la gare.
practice.explanation: Use nous avons plus couru.

practice.prompt: Supply the past participle of battre: L'équipe a ___ son record.
practice.explanation: Battre gives battu, not batté.

practice.prompt: Use apparaître in the passé composé with être: Une ligne ___ sur l'écran.
practice.explanation: Ligne is feminine singular, so apparue agrees.

practice.prompt: Supply reconnaître in the passé composé: Vous ___ sa voix.
practice.explanation: Recognu is not the participle; use reconnu.

practice.prompt: Use paraître meaning seem in the passé composé: Cette solution ___ simple.
practice.explanation: Paraître meaning seem takes avoir and paru.

practice.prompt: Supply the past participle of parcourir: Elles ont ___ le quartier à pied.
practice.explanation: Parcourir shares couru's pattern; do not agree with elles.

practice.prompt: Supply combattre in the passé composé: Les associations ___ cette injustice.
practice.explanation: The derivative retains battu: combattu.

practice.prompt: Use apparaître with être: Plusieurs fissures ___ hier. Supply the passé composé; une fissure is feminine.
practice.explanation: Être and a feminine plural subject require apparues.

practice.prompt: Supply naître in the passé composé: Les jumelles ___ en août.
practice.explanation: Naître takes être and the feminine plural participle nées.

practice.prompt: Supply disparaître in the passé composé using avoir: Les nuages ___.
practice.explanation: Disparaître gives disparu.

practice.prompt: Supply accourir in the passé composé with avoir: Tu ___ pour nous aider.
practice.explanation: Accourir gives accouru; the prompt specifies the accepted avoir construction.

practice.prompt: Supply recourir in the passé composé: Nous ___ à un interprète.
practice.explanation: Recourir à means to resort to or use the services of.

practice.prompt: Supply the participle of débattre: Vous avez ___ du budget.
practice.explanation: The family participle is débattu.

practice.prompt: Use apparaître with être in the passé composé: Vous ___ à la télévision. Address one woman politely.
practice.explanation: Polite singular vous takes êtes but feminine singular agreement.

practice.prompt: Choose both accepted auxiliaries for a published book: Ce roman ___ paru l'an dernier.
practice.explanation: Publication allows either a paru or est paru; paraître does not always exclude être.

practice.prompt: Supply méconnaître in the passé composé: Nous ___ l'importance du problème.
practice.explanation: Méconnaître gives méconnu and means fail to appreciate or understand here.

practice.prompt: Supply reparaître in the passé composé with avoir: Le défaut ___ après la réparation.
practice.explanation: Reparaître gives reparu: the defect reappeared.

practice.prompt: Supply comparaître in the passé composé: Les témoins ___ devant le tribunal.
practice.explanation: Comparaître gives comparu and means appear in court.

practice.prompt: Supply secourir in the passé composé: Les bénévoles ___ les voyageurs bloqués.
practice.explanation: Secourir follows the couru participle family.

practice.prompt: Supply abattre in the passé composé: Le vent ___ un vieil arbre.
practice.explanation: Abattre retains battu after its prefix.

practice.prompt: Supply se battre in the passé composé: Elles ___ pour obtenir une bibliothèque.
practice.explanation: The reflexive construction uses être and feminine plural agreement, unlike avoir + battu.

production_task.prompt: Describe a walking tour where you recognized someone and noticed something new. Use a connaître-family participle, a courir-family participle and apparaître with être. Include a feminine plural subject for one agreement.
production_task.model_answer: Nous avons parcouru le vieux quartier. J'ai reconnu une ancienne voisine près du marché. Deux fresques sont apparues sur le mur depuis ma dernière visite. Elles ont paru très lumineuses au soleil.
production_task.translation: We walked through the old neighbourhood. I recognized a former neighbour near the market. Two murals have appeared on the wall since my last visit. They looked very bright in the sunlight.
rubric: Do not agree avoir participles with the subject.
Agree the être participle with the intended subject.
Tell a connected event rather than a list of unrelated forms.
